arxiv-2103-01904.title: A Spectral Enabled GAN for Time Series Data Generation
arxiv-2103-01904.creator: Kaleb Smith, Anthony O. Smith
arxiv-2103-01904.description: Abstract Time dependent data is a main source of information in today’s data driven world. Generating this type of data though has shown its challenges and made it an interesting research area in the field of generative machine learning. One such approach was that by Smith et al.

arxiv-2106-12185.title: Numerical Simulation of Noise in Pulsed Brillouin Scattering Journal: josab
arxiv-2106-12185.creator: Oscar A. Nieves, Matthew D. Arnold, Michael. J. Steel, Mikołaj K. Schmidt, Christopher G. Poulton
arxiv-2106-12185.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Oscar A. Nieves, Matthew D. Arnold, Michael. J. Steel, Mikołaj K. Schmidt, Christopher G. Poulton. We present a numerical method for modelling noise in Stimulated Brillouin Scattering (SBS). The model applies to dynamic cases such as optical pulses, and accounts for both thermal noise and phase noise from the input lasers.

arxiv-2112-08369.title: Feature-Attending Recurrent Modules for Generalization in Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2112-08369.creator: Wilka Carvalho Andrew Lampinen, Kyriacos Nikiforou Felix Hill Murray Shanahan, [2pt] Harvard University Google DeepMind
arxiv-2112-08369.description: Abstract Many important tasks are defined in terms of objects. To generalize across these tasks, a reinforcement learning (RL) agent needs to exploit the structure that the objects induce. Prior work has either hard-coded object-centric features, used complex object-centric generative models, or updated state using local spatial features. However, these approaches have had limited success in enabling general RL agents.

arxiv-2307-16609.title: Noisy Self-Training with Data Augmentations for Offensive and Hate Speech Detection Tasks
arxiv-2307-16609.creator: João A. Leite, Carolina Scarton, Diego F. Silva
arxiv-2307-16609.description: Abstract Online social media is rife with offensive and hateful comments, prompting the need for their automatic detection given the sheer amount of posts created every second. Creating high-quality human-labelled datasets for this task is difficult and costly, especially because non-offensive posts are significantly more frequent than offensive ones. However, unlabelled data is abundant, easier, and cheaper to obtain.

arxiv-2405-17892.title: Data-Driven Predictive Control and MPC: Do we achieve optimality?
arxiv-2405-17892.creator: A.S. Anand, S. Sawant, D. Reinhardt, S. Gros
arxiv-2405-17892.description: Abstract In this paper, we explore the interplay between Predictive Control and closed-loop optimality, spanning from Model Predictive Control to Data-Driven Predictive Control. Predictive Control in general relies on some form of prediction scheme on the real system trajectories. However, these predictions may not accurately capture the real system dynamics, for e.g., due to stochasticity, resulting in sub-optimal control policies.

arxiv-2410-07521.title: Measures of intermediate pressures for geometric Lorenz attractors
arxiv-2410-07521.creator: Yi Shi, Xiaodong Wang
arxiv-2410-07521.description: Abstract Pressure measures the complexity of a dynamical system concerning a continuous observation function. A dynamical system is called to admit the intermediate pressure property if for any observation function, the measure theoretical pressures of all ergodic measures form an interval.

arxiv-2503-24071.title: From Colors to Classes: Emergence of Concepts in Vision Transformers
arxiv-2503-24071.creator: Teresa Dorszewski tksc@dtu.dk, Lenka Tětková lenhy@dtu.dk, Robert Jenssen robert.jenssen@uit.no, Lars Kai Hansen lkai@dtu.dk, Kristoffer Knutsen Wickstrøm kristoffer.k.wickstrom@uit.no 1 Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, Technical University of Denmark2 Department of Physics an
arxiv-2503-24071.description: Abstract Vision Transformers (ViTs) are increasingly utilized in various computer vision tasks due to their powerful representation capabilities. However, it remains understudied how ViTs process information layer by layer. Numerous studies have shown that convolutional neural networks (CNNs) extract features of increasing complexity throughout their layers, which is crucial for tasks like domain adaptation and transfer learning.

arxiv-2509-19998.title: Conjugacy problem in T-RAAGs
arxiv-2509-19998.creator: Gemma Crowe, Islam Foniqi
arxiv-2509-19998.description: Abstract In this paper, we construct an implementable algorithm which solves the conjugacy problem in twisted right-angled Artin groups (T-RAAGs). In certain cases, the complexity is known to be linear, by reducing the problem to the twisted conjugacy problem in right-angled Artin groups. We also show that T-RAAGs are biautomatic, providing an alternative solution to the conjugacy problem.

arxiv-2511-18176.title: Optimality Conditions and Duality for Multiobjective Fractional Bilevel Optimization Problems
arxiv-2511-18176.creator: Felipe Lara, Rishabh Pandey, Vinay Singh
arxiv-2511-18176.description: Abstract This paper studies a multiobjective bilevel optimization problem where each objective is a fractional function. By reformulating the problem into a single-level one, we establish refined necessary and sufficient optimality conditions. These results are derived using ∂ D {\partial}_{D} -nonsmooth Abadie-type constraint qualifications and generalized convexity concepts (quasiconvexity and pseudoconvexity) based on directional convexificators.

arxiv-2605-04065.title: Free Energy-Driven Reinforcement Learning with Adaptive Advantage Shaping for Unsupervised Reasoning in LLMs
arxiv-2605-04065.creator: Yiming Huang, Zhenbo Shi, Xincheng Wen, Jichuan Zeng, Cuiyun Gao, Peiyi Han, Chuanyi Liu

pmc-11499797.title: Systematic review of variables that moderate and/or mediate the relationship between child maltreatment and adverse outcomes: a study protocol
pmc-11499797.creator: Denise Colley, Jenny Seidler, Lena Rasch, Britta Gahr, Lisa Küppers, Ertan Mayatepek, Freia De Bock
pmc-11499797.description: IntroductionChild maltreatment (CM) is associated with adverse cognitive, behavioural, physical and social outcomes that often continue until adulthood. Systematic reviews on mediators and moderators of this relationship mostly investigate childhood adversities in general or only with regard to an adult population, single outcomes or single forms of maltreatment.

pmc-11509889.title: The Significance of an Initial Controlling Nutritional Status Score in Predicting the Functional Outcome, Complications, and Mortality in a First-Ever Ischemic Stroke
pmc-11509889.creator: Hyoseon Choi, Yea Jin Jo, Min Kyun Sohn, Jongmin Lee, Yong-Il Shin, Gyung-Jae Oh, Yang-Soo Lee, Min Cheol Joo, So Young Lee, Min-Keun Song, Junhee Han, Jeonghoon Ahn, Young-Hoon Lee, Yun-Hee Kim, Won Hyuk Chang, Deog Young Kim, Susanna C Larsson
pmc-11509889.description: Background and Purpose: Nutritional status can influence the outcomes and mortality of various diseases. The association between initial nutritional status and ischemic stroke outcomes, however, remains poorly understood. This study investigated whether the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score at admission could predict functional recovery, complications, and survival following an ischemic stroke.

pmc-11520219.title: Cancer Survivors and Cardiovascular Risk: What Patients Should Know From the Perspective of Another Survivor
pmc-11520219.creator: Steven Petrow
pmc-11520219.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). w drug regimen flipped the odds, and after 5 years, I was deemed cured. I didn’t know there would be a health cost to that cure. One of those “costs” is cardiotoxicity. In other words, the cisplatin1 that saved my life is associated with a higher risk of cardiotoxicity, which can include myocardial infarction, coronary artery disease, heart failure, valve disease, and arrhythmias.

pmc-12396170.title: Symptoms and Risk Factors for Long COVID: A Cross‐Sectional Study in Primary Care
pmc-12396170.creator: Assel Muratovna Shigayeva Ferreira, Flávia Emília Leite de Lima Ferreira, Caio César Ferreira Alverga, João Agnaldo do Nascimento, André Luís Bonifácio de Carvalho, Gabriel Rodrigues Martins de Freitas, João Aurílio Cardoso de Moraes, Izabele da Silva Rocha, Lucas Tomaz da Silva, Beatriz Carolinny P
pmc-12396170.description: This study aimed to determine the occurrence and risk factors for persistent symptoms after mild to moderate severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) infection in patients who presented in primary care during the 2021 pandemic. A retrospective cross‐sectional survey was conducted in six public family health care units in Joao Pessoa, Brazil.

pmc-12565761.title: Phenotypic Expression of Respiratory Diseases and Tailored Treatment in Patients with Intermediate Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency: Evidence from a Retrospective Analysis of a Selected Cohort of Patients
pmc-12565761.creator: Anna Annunziata, Giuseppe Fiorentino, Francesca Simioli, Lidia Atripaldi, Marco Balestrino, Giacomo Zuccarini, Barbara Piras, Alessandro Libra, Fabio Pino, Pierpaolo Di Micco, Carmine Siniscalchi, Ilaria Ferrarotti, Luigi Aronne, Raffaella Manzo, Carlo Vancheri, Cecilia Calabrese
pmc-12565761.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Introduction: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a genetic condition caused by SERPINA1 variants with variable severity. Current international guidelines do not recommend augmentation therapy for intermediate AATD; nevertheless, some patients show clinically severe phenotypes in real-world practice. We aimed to evaluate, in an exploratory manner, the potential effects of augmentation therapy on exacerbations, quality of life, and lung function in this subgroup.

pmc-12594365.title: Nitrogen dioxide pollution in 346 Chinese cities: Spatiotemporal variations and natural drivers from multi-source remote sensing data
pmc-12594365.creator: Feifei Cheng, Qing Sun, Jiaqi Zhang, Jiahe Liu, Wenwen Lü, Fapeng Shen, Heming Yang, Benedetto Schiavo, Benedetto Schiavo, Benedetto Schiavo, Benedetto Schiavo, Benedetto Schiavo
pmc-12594365.description: In this study, tropospheric column concentration of nitrogen dioxide (TNO2CC) were derived from Sentinel-5P data. We employed statistical and local spatial autocorrelation analyses to investigate the spatialtemporal distribution and variation of TNO2CC across 346 major Chinese cities from 2019 to 2023.

pmc-12648699.title: Bacillus mycoides bacteremia after dog bite trauma in a patient on chronic suppressive antibiotics
pmc-12648699.creator: Caroline Diggins, Carissa Tedeschi, Julia Jandro, Kristen Hysell
pmc-12648699.description: Bacillus mycoides (B. mycoides) is a Gram-positive bacillus belonging to the Bacillaceae family, found in soil and plant rhizospheres. Infection of humans by B. mycoides is exceedingly rare, previously reported only twice in the literature. Here, we present a third case of B. mycoides infection, specifically a bloodstream infection in a patient following a dog bite to the hand.

pmc-13008502.title: Ca2+ signalling in cardiac muscle: the importance of balances
pmc-13008502.creator: Ernst Niggli, Ana M Gomez
pmc-13008502.description: In this narrative review, an example of a cardiac arrhythmia with a mechanistically appealing molecular pathomechanism is highlighted. This example will be used to delineate how recent basic science findings, which are summarized, can be used to obtain a deeper understanding of pathological behaviour from the molecular to the cellular level.

pmc-13271492.title: Estrogen impacts NOD2-dependent regulation of intestinal homeostasis
pmc-13271492.creator: Mckenna Eklund, Edan Foley, Ines Alvarez-Garcia, Ines Alvarez-Garcia, Ines Alvarez-Garcia, Ines Alvarez-Garcia
pmc-13271492.description: Mutations in the innate immune receptor NOD2 are the greatest single genetic risk factor for Crohn’s disease, yet the mechanisms by which NOD2 regulates intestinal homeostasis remain unclear. We used a CRISPR-generated zebrafish model to determine the impacts of NOD2 deficiency on intestinal health.
